plan.title: Whole-blood co-expression modules and case/control tracking
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 120 whole-blood RNA-seq samples (60 case vs 60 control, single batch, unpaired, raw Salmon gene-level counts, 12000 genes) with the research question asking which co-expression modules form across all 120 samples and which track case vs control status. The plan follows the Inflexa full_plan procedure for a population-scale (n=60/group) bulk RNA-seq cohort with a coexpression extra analysis: (1) sample-structure QC via blind VST/PCA/sample-distance heatmap to confirm no batch or outlier structure before network construction; (2) minimal low-count filtering (filterByExpr) and TMM normalization, shared as the common expression matrix for both the differential expression and the co-expression analyses; (3) the co-expression module discovery itself — signed WGCNA on the variance-stabilized matrix, soft-threshold picked by the scale-free topology criterion (R^2 approx 0.8), dynamic tree cut on the TOM dissimilarity for modules, module eigengenes correlated against the case/control trait (point-biserial / Kruskal on eigengene vs status) to identify which modules track status, and module membership (kME) to rank hub genes per module; (4) because each group holds 60 samples (>=50), the between-group differential expression control uses limma-voom with a fixed-effects linear model rather than a negative-binomial count model (DESeq2/edgeR overstate significance in large population cohorts per the grounded caution), giving a gene-level case-vs-control signal to cross-reference against the status-associated modules; (5) functional characterization of the case/control-associated module(s) — hub genes tested by ORA against Hallmark, Reactome, and WikiPathways human gene sets and a STRING-based PPI subnetwork view for interpretability; (6) an integrative report tying together which modules track status, their top hub genes, and their functional annotation, with the caveat that WGCNA module-trait correlations are exploratory/descriptive (no formal multiplicity-adjusted inferential claim per rule) and that co-expression module membership is not itself a hypothesis test of case/control effect — the limma-voom DE step is the inferential complement.
